criteria.description: Correctly splits off the s=t term from the sum.
Correctly applies Bellman's principle to identify the remaining sum's minimum as V_{t+1}(f(x,u_t)).
Correctly assembles the final Bellman equation.

solutions.fullSolution:
sum_{s=t}^T c(x_s,u_s)+phi(x_T) = c(x_t,u_t) + [sum_{s=t+1}^T c(x_s,u_s)+phi(x_T)].
By Bellman's principle, whatever u_t is chosen, the remaining decisions from t+1 onward must be optimal given the resulting state x_{t+1}=f(x_t,u_t); the minimum of the bracketed remaining-sum term is therefore exactly V_{t+1}(f(x,u_t)) by definition.
So V_t(x) = min_{u_t}[c(x,u_t) + V_{t+1}(f(x,u_t))], i.e. the Bellman equation V_t(x)=min_u[c(x,u)+V_{t+1}(f(x,u))].

criteria.description: Correctly computes dV/dx = 2x^T P(t) and substitutes into HJB.
Correctly minimizes over u, arriving at u*=-R^-1 B^T P(t) x.
Correctly substitutes back and argues matrix equality for all x to derive the Riccati equation.

solutions.fullSolution:
dV/dx = 2x^T P(t) (P symmetric, quadratic form gradient rule). HJB becomes: -x^T Pdot x = min_u[x^T Q x + u^T R u + 2x^T P(Ax+Bu)].
Minimize over u: d/du[u^T R u + 2x^T P B u] = 2u^T R + 2x^T P B = 0, giving u*^T = -x^T P B R^-1, i.e. u* = -R^-1 B^T P x.
Substitute back: -x^T Pdot x = x^T Q x + x^T P A x + x^T A^T P x - x^T P B R^-1 B^T P x (after using symmetry to combine the cross terms). Since this holds for all x, the matrices multiplying x on each side must match: -Pdot = A^T P + P A - P B R^-1 B^T P + Q.

c = m*sqrt(eps*rho) = 2*sqrt(2*0.5) = 2*sqrt(1) = 2. b = m*sqrt(rho*(2c+eps)) = 2*sqrt(0.5*(4+2)) = 2*sqrt(3) ~= 3.464. Kd = b/(rho*m) = 3.464/(0.5*2) = 3.464/1 = 3.464. (Independently verified by substituting the resulting P back into the ARE with NumPy: residual ~1e-16.)

criteria.description: Correctly identifies the shared 'control cost + task cost' squared-norm structure.
Correctly identifies what differs: the decision variable and hierarchy level (position/acceleration/whole trajectory/policy).

solutions.fullSolution: All four minimize a sum of squared-norm terms: a control/deviation cost (how much am I moving/acting/costing) plus a task cost (how far from the target). What differs is the decision variable and the level of the control hierarchy it operates at: IK optimizes a single configuration q (position level, one-shot); operational space control optimizes a single control u (acceleration/torque level, one-shot); optimal control optimizes an entire policy or trajectory over time; trajectory optimization directly optimizes a whole discretized configuration sequence q_{0:T}. These are the same regularized-least-squares idea applied at different levels of a control hierarchy, from a single instantaneous decision up to an entire trajectory, which is why the same Gauss-Newton/SQP solvers handle all of them.
